# Policymaker #300: iteration 0047

Status: done. I ordered one landing task. Wake is false.

## What changed and why
- Review #297 accepted the #292 readiness-case proposal for capability #169. All 6 sha256 values match. The proposal has property expectations only ([snapshot](../.github/loop/data/session-reports/297/1697341b9bf9d47e3dcb1bd4dad395debe8fabe594b7af2569527ab36b4d3d34.json)).
- Re-review #298 accepted the diagram-difference gap row (item A). It gave `revise` for the #281 split-checker fix (item B), because its own revert harness hid the results ([snapshot](../.github/loop/data/session-reports/298/fe6140844189b7a0026ae8bad4267dea32143d24484ceccf4453428d5d8a6ad7.json)).
- I measured item B in temporary copies. When I broke `TOKEN_VALUE_RE`, `split_boundary.py --check` exited 1. When I removed the partition check, it exited 1. When I moved the token mutation back to `value`, it exited 1. Thus the fix fails when it is reverted, and item B needs no new fix round.
- I wrote `execution/scripts/pin_readiness_300.py`. It is hash-gated and idempotent. It writes `benchmark/native/readiness-case.json` and pins it under the oracle milestone. It replaces the two "not re-reviewed" limitation sentences and re-pins `preparation-status.json`.
- I did two dry runs on a copy without LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT. Both runs gave the same bytes. The evaluator exited 0 with missing [] and 60 references. native_jobs, split_boundary, challenges, score and baseline `--check` exited 0.
- Order `pin-readiness-and-rereviews-300` (benchmark, low effort, 20 min / 25 turns, from main) runs the script once. Expected gain: main has the reviewed readiness case and current limitation text. Check: the evaluator shows 60 references, and the status sha256 is `4b0ec6da…`.

Gaps that stay open: capability #169 is not ready. No native LabVIEW run occurred. Controlled I/O has no expected values. All authors and reviewers in this chain are GPT-family models. The benchmark is not ready, and the owner has not accepted the method.

## What next
- Saved: the script, `.session/orders.json`, and `policy/working-memory.md` (section Iteration 0047).
- Next step: verify the landing on main, then delete `pin_readiness_300.py`. Then plan the review of the #268 readiness record. That record is only in the comments of issue #268.
- Do not repeat: the #297 hash checks or the item B revert measurements.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
